intended_object: The (normalized) greatest common divisor of the finite family f(b), b ∈ s, in a normalized GCD monoid, with gcd(∅) = 0. Inferred from the docstring and the name.
explanation: The body folds the binary GCDMonoid.gcd over s, mapping each element through f and starting from 0. This is the standard finite gcd. Because gcd 0 a = normalize a, the result is the normalized gcd, and the empty family gives 0 (every element divides 0), which is the usual convention. It is equivalent to Multiset.gcd (s.val.map f), as Mathlib proves in Finset.gcd_def. NormalizedGCDMonoid is needed because Finset.fold requires the operation to be commutative and associative as an actual equality. In a plain GCDMonoid, gcd is only determined up to associates (units), so that may fail. The index type β and the function f are fully general, so the generality is natural.
